typesense:trending.greeting:
The blast tore through the Vaqueros base and split the corridor in two. Rudy lay unconscious beneath shattered concrete on one side; she was still standing on the other. Alejandro looked between them once.

Then he chose Rudy.

She watched him drag his best friend toward the exit before smoke swallowed them both. There was no time to feel it. She found another route, kicked through a jammed door—and the ceiling collapsed. A burning beam pinned her legs as flames raced closer and her radio vanished beneath the wreckage.

Outside, Shadows fired after Alejandro until he disappeared beyond the compound with Rudy. Graves was ordering a pursuit when someone shouted, “Movement, second floor!”

Through a blackened window, he saw her pounding against the glass.

A Shadow raised his rifle. “Hostile.”

Graves slammed the barrel aside. “I know who she is.”

The window blew outward. Fire rolled across the opening, and she disappeared.

Shepherd’s order made her an enemy. Leaving her inside meant one fewer gun aimed at his men. It was clean. Sensible. Exactly what Commander Graves should do.

But hours ago she had stood beside him, trusted him, laughed at his goddamn jokes.

“Sir, the structure’s going!” a Shadow warned.

“Stupid, sentimental son of a bitch,” Graves snarled at himself—and ran.

Heat struck like a wall when he entered. Smoke erased the corridor behind him while ammunition cooked off somewhere deeper inside. The ceiling buckled overhead, but Graves pushed through the flames, kicking open doors and screaming her name.

“Answer me, darlin’!”

Only the fire answered. He turned through the smoke as another section of ceiling crashed behind him.

“Real smart, Graves,” he coughed bitterly. “Run into a collapsing building for a woman who’ll probably put a bullet in you herself.”

He shoved deeper into the wreckage, fury and panic burning hotter than the flames.

“Answer me!” he roared. “You wanna kill me, darlin’, you’re gonna have to live long enough to do it!”
